statements.t: Through four interconnected pillars (Menu, Consumer, Restaurant and People), the Company intends to generate more demand and deliver it more efficiently to drive growth by elevating taste and quality, deepening customer relationships, improving customer and restaurant experiences and redefining hospitality.

As part of the Strategy, the Company aims to gain approximately 1.5 percentage points of market share in both the chicken and beverage categories by the end of 2030, versus September 2026 share, while maintaining its leadership position in the beef category.
More broadly, value remains foundational to Menu > NEXT as the Company seeks to deliver the combination of great taste, quality, convenience and affordability that customers expect.
The Company intends to leverage its distinctive brand assets, customer insights, loyalty ecosystem and digital capabilities to provide greater value to customers.

Through these efforts, the Company expects to deliver approximately 250 basis points of gross restaurant-level efficiency gains as Restaurant > NEXT elements are fully deployed across the U.S. and International Operated Markets.

Through Make It Golden , a multi-year Systemwide commitment to elevate the customer experience through great food and great hospitality that are uniquely McDonald’s, the Company intends to build capabilities that can be taught, measured and scaled across the System, and that strengthen customer preference and encourage repeat visits.
The Company intends to deploy the Strategy with discipline, pairing globally scaled solutions with local market insights.

To support implementation of the Strategy, the Company plans to provide approximately $8.5 billion in total cash partnering support through the end of 2036, including approximately $5 billion in cash partnering by the end of 2030, through a combination of rent relief and capital support.
• The Company expects net restaurant unit expansion will contribute approximately 2.5% to 2026 Systemwide sales growth, in constant currencies.
• The Company expects full year 2026 Selling, general and administrative expenses of about 2.2% of Systemwide sales.
• The Company expects 2026 operating margin percent to be in the mid-to-high 40% range.

• Based on current interest and foreign currency exchange rates, the Company expects interest expense for the full year 2026 to increase between 4% and 6% driven primarily by higher average interest rates.
• The Company expects the effective income tax rate for the full year 2026 to be between 21% and 23%.
• The Company expects 2026 capital expenditures to be about $3.7 billion, with the majority directed towards new restaurant unit expansion across the U.S. and International Operated Markets.

Over the long-term, the Company expects to achieve the following financial targets.
• The Company expects net restaurant unit expansion will contribute nearly 2.5% to 2027 Systemwide sales growth, in constant currencies, moderating to about 2% by the end of 2030.
• The Company expects full year Selling, general and administrative expenses of about 1.9% of Systemwide sales by the end of 2030.
• The Company expects full year operating margin percent to be in the low-to-mid 50% range by the end of 2030.

• The Company expects about $3 billion of annual baseline capital expenditures plus $1.5 billion to $2 billion of cumulative capital partnering support to accelerate deployment of Restaurant > NEXT from 2027 through the end of 2030, based on current foreign currency exchange rates.
• The Company is targeting 50,000 global units by the end of 2028.
• The Company expects to achieve a full year free cash flow conversion rate in the mid-to-high 80% range by the end of 2030.

The various elements of our McDonald’s > NEXT strategy are expected to be implemented over a multi-year period, with timing and sequencing to vary across our markets based on, among other factors, customer needs, restaurant and technology readiness, local economic conditions and franchisee capacity.

If we are delayed or unsuccessful in evolving or executing against our strategies, including in the transition from Accelerating the Arches to McDonald’s > NEXT , if the execution of our strategies proves to be more difficult, costly or time consuming than expected, or if our strategies do not yield the desired results, our business, financial condition and results of operations may suffer.
If we do not anticipate and address industry trends and evolving consumer preferences and effectively execute our pricing, promotional, marketing and menu plans, our business could suffer.

To do so, we need to anticipate and respond effectively to continuously shifting consumer demographics and industry trends in sourcing, food and beverage preparation, menu offerings, and consumer behavior and preferences, including with respect to the use of digital channels, health and wellness trends and environmental and social responsibility matters.

Our ability to build upon our strengths and advantages also depends on the impact of pricing, promotional, marketing and menu plans across the System, and the ability to adjust these plans to respond quickly and effectively to evolving customer behavior and preferences, as well as shifting economic and competitive conditions.
Existing or future pricing strategies and marketing plans, as well as the value proposition they represent, are expected to continue to be important components of our business strategy.
Our investments to transform and enhance the customer experience, including through technology, training and hospitality initiatives, may not generate the expected results.

As part of these investments, we are continuing to place emphasis on improving our service model and strengthening relationships with customers, in part through digital channels and loyalty initiatives, mobile ordering and payment systems, and enhancing our drive thru technologies, which efforts may not generate expected results.

Our McDonald’s > NEXT strategy and Make It Golden hospitality elevation commitment also include investments in Systemwide training and generative AI-enabled technologies intended to improve the customer experience through great food and great hospitality via restaurant execution and efficiency, the success of which depends on franchisee alignment, workforce capabilities and effective adoption and deployment…
We face intense competition in our markets, which could hurt our business.

We expect our environment to continue to be highly competitive, and our results in any particular reporting period may be impacted by a contracting IEO segment or by new or continuing actions, product offerings, technologies or consolidation of our competitors and third-party partners, which may have short- and long-term impacts on our results.

There can be no assurance these strategies will be effective, and some strategies may be effective at improving some metrics while adversely affecting others, which could have the overall effect of harming our business.

Our operating performance could also be negatively affected if our franchisees experience food safety or other operational problems or project an image inconsistent with our brand and values, particularly if our contractual and other rights and remedies are limited, costly to exercise or subjected to litigation and potential delays.

If franchisees do not successfully operate restaurants in a manner consistent with our required standards, our brand’s image and reputation could be harmed, which in turn could hurt our business and operating results.
Further, adverse publicity resulting from claims may hurt our business.

Health epidemics or pandemics have in the past and may in the future impact macroeconomic conditions, consumer behavior, labor availability and supply chain management, as well as local operations in impacted markets, all of which can adversely affect our business, financial results and outlook.

The profitability of our Company-owned and operated restaurants depends in part on our ability to anticipate and react to changes in commodity costs, including food, paper, supplies, fuel and utilities, as well as distribution and other operating costs, including labor.

We have also experienced increased pressure from stakeholders to provide expanded disclosure and establish additional commitments, targets or goals, and take actions to meet them, which could expose us to additional market, operational, execution and reputational costs and risks.

dropped.t: Building on its foundational strength with burgers, the Company will continue to evolve and innovate its longest-standing menu item with plans to continue to implement “Best Burger”; a series of operational and formulation changes designed to deliver hotter, juicier, tastier burgers to nearly all markets by the end of 2026.

As another way to unlock further growth, the Company plans to continue to accelerate the pace of restaurant openings and technology innovation so that whenever and however customers choose to interact with McDonald’s, they can enjoy a fast, easy experience that meets their needs.
McDonald's loyalty customers have proven to be highly engaged, and the Company plans to increase its 90-day active users to 250 million by the end of 2027.
Further, the Company plans to grow its annual Systemwide sales to loyalty members to $45.0 billion by the end of 2027.
The Company continues to scale this capability and expects to increase the percentage of Systemwide delivery sales originating from our mobile app to 30% by the end of 2027.

◦ Restaurant Development: The Company will continue to accelerate the pace of restaurant openings to attempt to fully capture the demand being driven through our Strategy in many of our largest markets.
In 2026, the Company plans to open approximately 2,600 new restaurants (gross) across the globe, which will contribute to slightly over 4.5% new unit growth (net of closures).

Further, the Company continues to build on its industry-leading development, by progressing toward the targeted expansion to 50,000 restaurants by the end of 2027, which would make it the fastest period of restaurant unit growth in Company history.

Further, as part of the Company’s plans for long-term growth and solidifying McDonald’s leadership position, the Company will continue to develop and implement three technology-enabled platforms designed to build our competitive advantages, cement our place in culture and stay one step ahead of our customers’ expectations.

The Company intends to deploy new, universal software that all McDonald’s restaurants will run on, enabling restaurants to roll out innovation even faster, with less complexity and more reliability; and customers will enjoy a more familiar, consistent experience.
Globally, the Company expects to open approximately 2,600 restaurants.
The Company expects approximately 2,100 net restaurant additions in 2026.
